title: Long-horizon autonomy boundaries
summary: Long-horizon work MUST make continuous meaningful progress across bounded task failures while preserving every correctness, verification, review, and operator-authority boundary. Only the enumerated hard blocks stop a task.
instructions: The operator who selects long-horizon mode expects continuous meaningful progress, not excuses. An operator who returns to a long-horizon session MUST NOT find an open question, an operator-decision pause, or a deferred task waiting, except for a hard block this policy enumerates. Every other stop is a defect in the agent's reasoning or in the harness, because the operator selected this mode to be absent. The agent MUST treat it as one: decide, record the judgment, and continue.

Hard blocks are few and the list is closed: (1) an action an invariant reserves for the operator (push, publication, deployment, history rewrite, destructive reset, branch deletion, external release, or inventing an operator override); (2) a secret, credential, or authorization that is genuinely absent after the operator-question recovery flow; (3) a correctness or security failure that no permitted action can repair; (4) a destructive or irreversible action the operator did not direct. Nothing else is a hard block. A worker MUST NOT report `blocked`, and the harness MUST NOT stop a task, for any other reason, because an open-ended blocker class is what turns a long run into a queue of questions.

A criterion, ceiling, budget, bound, or cadence whose only backing is cost, speed, wall time, or convenience is never a long-horizon blocker, wherever it is written, including inside a ship criterion or an entry gate. An agent that meets one MUST take the smallest excess or the smallest source-allowed repair (raise the bound, waive the criterion with a recorded reason, or route the task past it), record the reason, and continue, because a cost rule protects nothing that duration can damage. A `blocked` outcome that cites such a rule is a governance defect, and the agent that records it MUST also record the repair it should have taken.

An agent MUST NOT cite this policy, the long-horizon handbook, a ladder rung, an invariant identifier, or a gate identifier as its reason to report `blocked`. Those texts consume blockers; they never create one, because a rule that manufactured its own blockers would defeat the mode it defines. Before writing `blocked`, an agent MUST answer one question from the operating principles and the operator's request: would this operator, who chose to be absent, expect the agent to decide this itself? When the answer is yes, the agent decides, records the judgment in its output, and continues.

An agent that caused the condition it faces (its own test run moved a rolling average, its own commit changed a fingerprint, its own edit broke a gate, its own retry spent a budget) MUST repair or absorb that condition itself. A self-caused condition is never an operator question and never a deferral reason, because the agent already holds every fact needed to resolve it.

A transient failure is a retry, never a deferral: an evaluator reply that does not parse, an executor timeout, an unavailable tool, a flaky gate sample, or a stale build. The harness MUST retry it within its bounds, and when a selected away option fails to apply it MUST fall through to the next permitted ranked option before it defers a task, because a transient signature says nothing about the work.

The operator's chat session MUST supervise a long-horizon session end to end: the queue, every task run it opens, and every run a task's plan approval routes to (a delivery run, cohort chunk runs advanced in parallel, and the release run). A task MUST finish only when its route finishes, never when its planning run does, because a run whose fan-out nobody supervises is work the session has silently dropped. The harness performs the mechanical part of every wake (ladder, the one scoped re-plan, route tracking, cohort start and release, task completion) and returns everything else to the supervisor's reasoning.

Cursor-owned conversation summarization is the supervisor's context boundary. The supervisor MUST rebuild from the durable session record and each run's state after a summary rather than from memory, because the record is what survives. Only a session a scheduled job drives with no chat open runs in harness driver processes, whose per-task restart is their boundary.

No function ends a long-horizon task. A harness verdict (a rejected ranking, a spent decision budget, an apply error, an evaluator reply that did not parse, an exhausted ladder, an operator-only mark, an executor failure) is evidence for the session arbiter, never a deferral by itself, because a mechanical verdict cannot tell a hard block from an edge case nobody anticipated. The harness MUST pass every stop that is not a terminal success to the arbiter before any deferral is written.

The session's arbiter is whoever supervises it: the operator's chat session when one drives the session, and the harness arbiter only for a session a scheduled job drives with no chat open. The arbiter MUST reason from the operating principles and the operator's request against the four hard blocks, and its default is override. It MUST defer a task only by naming the hard block it confirmed, because a deferral without a named hard block is the harness manufacturing a stop. When the harness arbiter cannot produce an applicable verdict, the harness MUST apply a deterministic re-attempt and arbitrate the next stop again, and a task that still recurs past the override bound is recorded as a harness failure, never as an operator-owned block.

Every deferral record MUST carry its classification: the hard block the arbiter named with its reasoning, a harness failure, or the operator's own defer command. A supervisor who reviews the record after the run MUST reinstate any deferral whose hard block it does not confirm and any harness failure it can route past, because the review is the last reasoning layer and a deferral it lets stand is its own decision.
Added autonomy MUST NOT lower verification, review depth, correctness, security, or maintainability because longer execution is useful only when its evidence stays trustworthy.

The recorded involvement selection and its snapshotted contract are the entire mode definition. Agents MUST NOT infer extra authority from the long-horizon name, because current models can overgeneralize from labels.
Every invariant listed in the long-horizon handbook MUST survive unchanged because autonomy cannot trade away operator authority or repository safety.

An unattended gate decision MUST come only through the existing evaluator, guardrails, and immutable ledger. This route is required because a second decision path could bypass the operator-defined bounds.

An agent MUST still escalate rather than assume when required information or authority is genuinely unavailable, which is one of the enumerated hard blocks and nothing wider. A session MUST route that task to the deferred ledger and request inbox. The session MUST NOT wait, because the operator is absent between preflight and post-run.
A blocker or pause MUST end the affected task rather than the task collection. The harness MUST count retry bounds per task, because one failure must not consume another task's budget.
The bounded escalation ladder MUST replace the same-signature pause for a task because a repeated failure should change strategy before the task is deferred.

An integrating agent MAY exclude a failing unit only with a recorded reason, a follow-up item, and exclusion of its dependents. Those conditions exist because the remaining independent units must keep valid dependency evidence.

A prompt task MUST receive only its workspace and its own session runtime directory by default because an unattended launch must not inherit unrelated write reach. Its evidence MUST record those granted roots and its tool policy. The task MUST either be denied every write outside those roots by the host, with that enforcement recorded, or have every path it changed outside them recorded as an unapproved change that fails the task. An observation that excludes a tree from that recording MUST NOT report a clean scope result. A wider harness-root grant MUST be explicit and named, and a declared workspace MUST NOT resolve to the harness root.

instructions.text: A supervisor MUST write run-level waste into the durable run record. That waste is what a relaxed gate surfaces in chat. The record exists because post-run review needs the same evidence without a mid-run interruption.

guidance_sources.read_trigger: Read this guidance before you act on a long-horizon run or session.
